summary: The change adds guards against duplicate-key dictionary inserts in TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo and adds tests for SuppressSourceGeneration = true validation, but it inverts the mixed-key-detection condition at TypeCollector.cs lines 1005 and 1145. On head this crashes the analyzer (AD0001/NullReferenceException) on mixed int/string keys, emits false MsgPack005 diagnostics and drops members 2+ from generated formatters for every multi-key type, producing 34 new full-suite failures. The duplicate-key crash is fixed, but the mixed-key crash from base is not resolved and a broad regression is introduced; build passes and fail-without-fix was not run. Overall: blocker, do not merge until the condition is reverted and tests re-run.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: All three F1-listed tests pass on head: missing-[Key] (MsgPack004), non-MessagePackObject member type (MsgPack003), and AllowPrivate required (MsgPack015) are all reported for suppressed types. The mixed-key-kind example named in F1's text is exercised under N1 and crashes there.

Its covering test expects zero diagnostics for a suppressed type, but head reports a false MsgPack005 mixed-key diagnostic for Prop1, so the no-extra-diagnostics requirement is not demonstrated (the failure is the same inverted condition bug, not an F2-category diagnostic).

MixedKeyKindsAreReportedWithoutAnalyzerFailure crashes with AD0001 instead of reporting MsgPack005, and tests.full_suite fails with 34 new failures, so the analyzer/generator still crashes on invalid contracts in suppressed types.
tests.fail_without_fix was not run, so it is unconfirmed that the new tests fail without the fix, and tests.full_suite has 34 regressions not present on base, violating the no-regression clause.

findings.title: Mixed-key detection condition inverted; analyzer crashes on mixed int/string keys
findings.claim: TypeCollector.cs lines 1005 and 1145 use `(isIntKey && stringKey == null) || (!isIntKey && intKey == null)`, the inverse of the base condition. For a mixed type (int key then string key) no diagnostic is emitted and execution falls through to `intKey!.Value`/member.IntKey with a null key, throwing NullReferenceException (reported as analyzer crash AD0001). Base had the same crash at the unguarded `intMembers.Add`, so the change does not resolve the mixed-key crash from issue #2234.

evidence.quote: continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.

findings.suggested_fix: Restore the base condition `(isIntKey && intKey == null) || (!isIntKey && stringKey == null)` at both sites; keep the `continue` and the `ContainsKey` guards.

findings.title: Same inverted condition reports false MsgPack005 and drops members 2+ from generated output
findings.claim: For any type with two or more same-kind keys, the second and later members satisfy `stringKey == null` (int keys) or `intKey == null` (string keys), so the condition falsely reports DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys (MsgPack005) and the `continue` skips the `intMembers.Add`/`stringMembers.Add`. Generated formatters omit members after the first, and analyzer tests see spurious MsgPack005 diagnostics.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the base condition `(isIntKey && intKey == null) || (!isIntKey && stringKey == null)` at both sites; keep the `continue` and the `ContainsKey` guards.

findings.suggested_fix: Revert the condition flip, re-run fail-without-fix and the full suite, and require zero new failures before merge.
